trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up-right.
The line must go down-right: left is number 13, which comes later.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (3,0) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,2). So the line goes down-left.
I can't rule out down-left or up-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-left.

Contradiction! Going up-right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (down-left from number 5) was wrong, so the line must go up-left.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
I can't rule out down-left or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-left.
Going up-left would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going left would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down-right.
Cell (0,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,0). So the line goes up-right.
The line must go up-left: left is number 17, which comes later.
I can't rule out up-right, up-left or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up-right.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,-1). So the line goes up-right.
Going up-left would force the line onto number 13 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards; going down-left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,-1). So the line goes up-right.
Going up-left would turn number 13 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down-right would wall in number 18, the last number. So the line goes down-left.
Going right would wall in number 18, the last number. So the line goes down-right.
Going up-right would wall in number 18, the last number; going right would strand number 15: it would be left with only one free neighbour (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going right would cut off the middle (3 cells). So the line goes down-right.
Cell (-3,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
